title: Discounted charity gala on a peak Saturday
question: A charity wants a peak Saturday in December for a 250-person gala at 40% below standard rate, offering profile in return. Do we take it?

options.label: Accept the booking at the rate offered
Counter with a minimum spend and a reduced discount
Decline and hold the date for full-rate demand

claims.statement: The equivalent December Saturday sold at full rate in each of the last two years.
At the proposed rate, contribution after direct costs is 9% against a 34% average.
The organiser states the gala is attended by roughly 40 corporate sponsors.
Sponsor attendance is assumed to generate future corporate bookings.
No charity event at this venue in three years has produced a traced corporate booking.
The organiser confirmed the charity board must approve any minimum spend commitment.

unknowns.question: What minimum spend would the charity board actually approve?

hidden.actual_decision_label: Counter with a minimum spend and a reduced discount
hidden.reasoning_notes: SYNTHETIC. Profile is not conversion, and a peak date at 9% contribution is a loss disguised as a booking. But declining outright discards a low-cost, reversible counter that keeps a 250-person event and 40 sponsors in play. Counter first; decline only if the board refuses.
